response.sql: WITH rc AS (SELECT d.A3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM disp p JOIN account a ON a.account_id = p.account_id JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id GROUP BY d.A3), sh AS (SELECT region, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM rc), av AS (SELECT region, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM sh) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_average_share FROM av WHERE share > avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: Each disp row is one client-account link, so counting disp rows per region counts a client once per account link. The region comes from the account's branch district (account.district_id), not the client's own district.
The average share across regions is the unweighted mean of the regions' shares, taken over regions that have at least one link. This equals 1 divided by the number of regions.

'On average how far their share is above the average share' is the mean of (share - average share) over the above-average regions, as a plain difference in share (not a ratio). The result is not rounded.
